Third-party provenance and license inventory

Source c854aed

This inventory records evidence inspected during release and website preparation on 2026-10-27 through 2026-10-29. It is not a completed redistribution approval. The root MIT license applies to independently authored project code and documentation; it does not relicense NRPE, distribution packaging, embedded code, dependencies, or public signing keys.

The active target was corrected to SLES 12 SP3 after receiving its actual OS/binary/library identity on 2026-10-28. The same reviewed NRPE/user sources are rebuilt natively; their previous SLE-15 runtime observations do not prove SLE-12 compatibility. The port additionally builds the macros from pinned upstream sources and retains their BSD notice. Original SLE-12 dependency RPMs are verified but are not release assets. Historical releases are unchanged.

Components in generated packages and sources

Component Evidence inspected Findings and remaining work
Debian nagios-nrpe Actual debian/copyright from the reconstructed custom sources for Debian 11 (4.0.3-1), 12 (4.1.0-1), and 13/14 (4.1.3-1); compared with the Debian 12 installed-package notice These four copyright files are identical. They declare GPL-2-or-later with an explicit OpenSSL linking exception for the main code; separate entries cover ACL code, snprintf, and Debian packaging. The full GPL text and upstream notice files are retained in the source archives. Recheck actual sources for every candidate; this is not a blanket approval of future source versions.
SLES NRPE 4.1.1 Pinned source manifest, revision 835292739a5736a9d8f0460f670b6f15; actual upstream archive, modified spec and existing custom binary's license output Resolved: src/utils.c:display_license() explicitly allows compilation, linking and use with OpenSSL and grants GPLv2-or-later. This is evidence from the SLES source itself. The earlier search missed the word "exemption". Preserve the upstream notice and full GPL text; see the source review.
NRPE ACL implementation Full license notices in include/acl.h and src/acl.c in the pinned SLES archive; Debian copyright entry Resolved: both full grants explicitly permit GPLv2 or later, consistent with Debian's notice. The short GPLv2 headings did not establish a GPLv2-only restriction. Retain Kaspersky Lab ZAO's 2011 copyright and the full per-file notices.
NRPE snprintf implementation src/snprintf.c in SLES upstream source; Debian copyright entry Patrick Powell, 1995. Permission requires retaining the source attribution notice. Do not replace it with the project's MIT notice.
Autoconf macros and generated helper files in NRPE sources Actual macros/LICENSE, macro headers, build-aux/config.guess, and build-aux/config.sub in the SLES source archive GPL notices include file-specific Autoconf/build-output exceptions. Preserve the files and their notices in the source package. These exceptions are not evidence of an OpenSSL linking exception for NRPE.
Nagios RPM macros 0.14 Immutable OBS revision a911087cc73b87e04465861110d43754; actual nagios-rpm-macros-COPYING and spec BSD-3-Clause, Lars Vogdt 2011. Retain the verbatim BSD notice, source RPM and complete original source set. The binary is a native build dependency, not a released runtime package.
SUSE NRPE packaging Actual pinned nrpe.spec, including its SUSE LLC 2024 header Spec header retains contributed changes under the pristine package's license, subject to its stated fallback. Keep the original notice and modified spec in the source RPM; the project MIT license does not replace the spec's terms.
system-user-nagios 1.0.0-0 Pinned manifest, revision b979817ae6424675519c86e80add617a; actual original spec extracted from the source RPM and hash-verified Resolved: the source spec itself explicitly declares MIT and retains the SUSE LLC 2024 copyright/licensing header. The missing standalone full text is supplied as a downstream companion notice, not represented as an original upstream file or a new project license grant. Preserve the spec and README and include that notice in release assets.

The SLES upstream archive is bound by SHA-256 7689aea570596573919371f7d6a1753eca90213368ede51f477e25782eb1ef9c. The manifests retain expected sizes and checksums for the original OBS input files; the exported source RPM contains the intentionally modified build spec.

The earlier NRPE source RPM was unpacked and compared with the pinned manifest: 14 entries matched (including the intentionally modified spec), while the OBS history file nrpe.changes was absent. The companion source RPM matched its spec and README; system-user-nagios.changes was absent. Record these provenance differences explicitly. New SLES builds now export the complete original OBS input sets under obs-sources/; release preparation verifies every file against the pinned manifests and includes the history alongside the SRPMs. The original comparison alone is not evidence of a fresh build.

The Debian 4.2.0-1 source review additionally covers the version now supplied by Debian 14. Its license grants and OpenSSL exception are unchanged; the Debian copyright edit removes obsolete FSF postal addresses. This does not approve later versions.

Reviewed Debian upstream archive and license-file hashes are recorded in packaging/debian-license-review.json. Automatic publication fails for a new source version or changed evidence until it is reviewed; source discovery and local builds remain dynamic. This separates successful compilation from license review of previously unexamined source bytes.

Host-only optional menu dependencies

requirements-menu.txt pins prompt-toolkit==3.0.52 and wcwidth==0.2.13. These libraries are downloaded by the user through pip; they are not vendored into this checkout or installed in the NRPE server package. The exact pinned wheels were downloaded without installation and their actual notices inspected:

Distribution License evidence Wheel SHA-256
prompt_toolkit-3.0.52-py3-none-any.whl prompt_toolkit-3.0.52.dist-info/licenses/LICENSE: BSD three-clause terms, Jonathan Slenders, 2014 9aac639a3bbd33284347de5ad8d68ecc044b91a762dc39b7c21095fcd6a19955
wcwidth-0.2.13-py2.py3-none-any.whl wcwidth-0.2.13.dist-info/LICENSE: MIT, Jeff Quast, 2014; additional Markus Kuhn 2007 permission/warranty notice 3da69048e4540d84af32131829ff948f1e022c1c6bdb8d6102117aac784f6859

Before distributing a bundled Python application, include these actual license files and inventory any additional shipped dependencies. Do not substitute the license files of different versions installed in a development environment.

requirements-audit.txt separately pins the optional CI/development tool pip-audit==2.10.1. Its installed distribution's actual licenses/LICENSE contains Apache License 2.0. It and its dependencies are installed separately for auditing, not vendored into this repository or shipped inside NRPE packages. Bundling this tool would require its own complete dependency/notice inventory. GitHub Actions are similarly fetched by CI at maintainer-selected upstream major-version tags rather than distributed as part of the server packages.

Build and runtime dependencies

requirements-website.txt pins the separate build-only renderer Markdown==3.8.2 (Python-Markdown). Its installed wheel's markdown-3.8.2.dist-info/licenses/LICENSE.md was inspected and contains BSD-3-Clause terms; wheel metadata records the same SPDX expression. The renderer is installed separately, not vendored, bundled into NRPE packages or copied into the static site. Generated pages retain the licenses of their original documentation and notices. Bundling the renderer would require its actual license text and a separate dependency inventory. Website CSS, templates and browser JavaScript are independently authored project code; no external JavaScript framework or analytics SDK is shipped. The locally hosted font and its retained notice are listed below.

The build-only syntax highlighter is shiki@4.5.0, pinned with integrity-checked transitive dependencies in website/package-lock.json. Installed shiki, @shikijs/core, @shikijs/langs, @shikijs/themes and @shikijs/engine-oniguruma LICENSE files were inspected and contain MIT terms; the installed @shikijs/vscode-textmate LICENSE.md also contains MIT terms. The original Shiki license is retained unchanged. Individual language/theme provenance is covered by the upstream grammar/theme notices. These dependencies, their grammars and WASM remain build-only, not vendored or included in NRPE packages or browser JavaScript. Generated code colors use the bundled GitHub Dark Default theme. The small NRPE syntax grammar and static HTML/CSS adapter are independently authored project code. The upstream NRPE sample configuration is referenced, not copied or relicensed as project code. Static diagrams use build-only mermaid@12.2.0 (MIT; the installed LICENSE was inspected and is retained unchanged) and puppeteer@25.16.0 (Apache-2.0 in its package metadata), also locked with integrity hashes. The renderer uses the workstation's installed Chrome/Chromium and ships SVG output, not a browser binary, Mermaid runtime, fonts or Node dependencies. The previous Pygments renderer dependency has been removed.

Docker images, OpenSSL, system libraries, Debian/SUSE repository packages, monitoring plugins, and SLES installation media retain their own licenses. The current release scope is the custom server packages, the SLES user package, their corresponding sources, and this project's build workflow. It does not include container images, dependency RPM/DEB bundles, or installation media. Any expansion requires an inventory of the additional shipped bytes.

The bundled SUSE public key is trust material identified by the fingerprints and checksums in the SLES manifests. They are not independently authored project code; do not label them MIT merely because they are in this repository. Retain their issuer identity and provenance.

Required release notices

Each candidate must include this inventory, the project MIT license, and the actual notices from the source packages being distributed. Source archives must retain their full upstream and distribution license files. The generic GitHub repository source archive does not replace corresponding NRPE sources.

For SLES, include the prepared notice directory as separate release assets alongside the unchanged binary and source RPMs. The review closes the previously recorded SLES OpenSSL, ACL-version and companion-MIT evidence gaps. It does not replace final candidate completeness and provenance checks.

Keep the project's unofficial-build wording and NRPE's LEGAL trademark notice. No endorsement or support entitlement from Nagios, Debian, or SUSE is implied. Metadata labels alone do not establish that an arbitrary release bundle retains all required notices. See the release plan.

Self-hosted website font

The website bundles Inter Variable from the official Inter project, licensed under SIL OFL 1.1. The verbatim notice is retained as website/assets/Inter-OFL.txt alongside InterVariable.woff2; the font is served locally and is not an NRPE dependency. No JetBrains font files, logos or illustrations are distributed.
